newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Fabian Alarcon named Ecuador's new president.
newsitem.headline: Fabian Alarcon named Ecuador's new president.

text.p: Ecuador's Congress voted on Tuesday to name its leader, Fabian Alarcon, as the country's new president, for the second time in a week.

The vote was passed by a 57-2 majority, with five abstentions and one blank vote, in the 82-member Congress and signalled an end to Ecuador's bizarre political crisis triggered by last week's ouster of populist leader Abdala Bucaram.
The election of the 49-year-old Alarcon for an interim period of 18 months capped a chaotic week in Ecuadorean politics, which at one point saw three people claiming the presidency.
The week's political turmoil started on Thursday with the dismissal by a divided Congress of Bucaram, a quirky populist whose antics earned him the nickname "El Loco" (the madman).

Carnival-like confusion ensued, with the defiant Bucaram refusing to step down, and doing so only when the military withdrew its support. In turn, Vice President Rosalia Arteaga appeared to cling to power, claiming it was constitutionally hers.
Alarcon, Ecuador's 41st president in the country's 167-year history, is to hand over power on Aug. 10, 1998, to a new democratically elected head of state, after general elections early next year.
